name: Cambridge
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Cambridge, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Cambridge, MA: Holiday on Ice in Kendall Square, the Longfellow House open house, a Polar Express movie day and Harvard Square lights.
lede: Cambridge celebrates Christmas in every square: a free ice show and Santa photos in Kendall Square, a candlelit open house in George Washington's old headquarters on Brattle Street, a Polar Express movie morning at CambridgeSide and the Charles Hotel's tree lighting in Harvard Square.
celebrates: Cambridge's holiday season is spread across its squares. In Harvard Square, The Charles Hotel opens the season with its annual tree lighting, and the Harvard Square Holiday Fair returns for two December weekends. On Brattle Street, the National Park Service decorates the Longfellow House for a free Holiday Open House with luminaria and harp music. In Kendall Square, the Canal District Kendall Winter Market brings free skating, Santa photos and the annual Holiday on Ice show, with Cambridge Arts' Winter Art Market alongside. CambridgeSide adds a free Polar Express movie day, and West Cambridge holds its Observatory Hill and Huron Village Holiday Stroll.
lastyear: In 2025 The Charles Hotel held its 40th tree lighting in Harvard Square on November 29, with live holiday music and a Mailbox for Santa where children dropped off letters for the North Pole. Cambridge Arts held its Holiday Art Market on December 13 and 14 as part of the Canal District Kendall Winter Market, which offered professional figure skating shows and family photos with Santa and Elsa. On December 20 the Cambridge Program staged its original play The Big Christmas Show.
facts: The Longfellow House on Brattle Street was built in 1759 for John Vassall. George Washington used it as his headquarters during the Siege of Boston in 1775 and 1776, and the National Park Service says the phrase the United States of America first appeared in writing there on January 2, 1776. Three generations of the Longfellow family lived in the house from 1837 to 1950, and the poet Henry Wadsworth Longfellow raised his children there.
trains: Cambridge is well connected by rail. The MBTA Fitchburg Line stops at Porter, one stop from North Station, and the Red Line runs through the city, with the MIT Museum right next to the Kendall/MIT station. Alewife, at the end of the Red Line, is where the Minuteman Bikeway begins on the old Boston and Maine rail line. For a holiday train ride, Edaville in Carver runs a train through the Christmas lights.

kidfact: George Washington lived and worked in a house on Brattle Street in Cambridge for about nine months in 1775 and 1776. Years later the poet Henry Wadsworth Longfellow and his children lived in the very same house.
faq: Where can kids see Santa in Cambridge?

Santa poses for photos at the Canal District Kendall Winter Market in Kendall Square, and Mr. and Mrs. Claus visit CambridgeSide's Polar Express movie day. At the Longfellow House Holiday Open House, children can read the Longfellow children's own letters to Santa from long ago.
Is there free ice skating in Cambridge at Christmas?

Yes. During the Canal District Kendall Winter Market in mid-December, Skate @ Canal District Kendall offers free skating admission all day and a free Holiday on Ice show by professional skaters. Skate rentals are charged at the rink's regular rates.
When is the Charles Hotel tree lighting?

The Charles Hotel holds its tree lighting in Harvard Square on the Saturday after Thanksgiving. In 2025 it was the 40th lighting, on November 29, with live holiday music and a Mailbox for Santa where children could drop off their letters for the North Pole. The Cambridge Office for Tourism lists it as free.
How do we get to Cambridge holiday events by train?

The MBTA Fitchburg Line stops at Porter, one stop from North Station, and the Red Line serves Harvard, Central, Kendall/MIT and Alewife. The MIT Museum sits right next to the Kendall/MIT station, a short walk from the Canal District Kendall rink.
